ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Martin Luther King Jr. Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for exhaustion, poor sleep and low mood: history, examination, ECG, blood tests, depression, anxiety, PTSD and safety screening, tobacco and blood pressure assessment, and a psychiatry referral. Concerns: He is exhausted and sleeps badly, and fears that if he slows down the movement will lose ground; He worries that a psychiatric diagnosis or medicine could be used against him and the movement, and wants his records kept private; He wants to stop smoking before his children see him smoke. [S]

list.item: Baptist minister and the president of a national civil rights organization; travels most weeks, speaks several times a day, and works late into the night [S]
Married, with four young children; lives in Atlanta; his faith and his congregation are central to his life [S]

Tobacco: about a pack of cigarettes a day since his twenties, kept out of public view and away from his children; has never tried to quit with help. Alcohol: occasional, AUDIT-C 2. No other drugs [S]
Racism and segregation have shaped his daily life, his work and his family's safety; he has been jailed repeatedly for nonviolent protest [S]

Two-week review and psychiatry consultation: diagnosis, safety, therapy and medicine

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Psychiatry consultation in two weeks to confirm the diagnosis, assess for PTSD and safety, and advise on therapy and medicine

Assessment at intake: blood count, metabolic panel, TSH, lipids, hemoglobin A1c and ECG; PHQ-9, GAD-7, PC-PTSD-5 and AUDIT-C; Insomnia Severity Index and sleep apnea screening; safety plan with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number
Tobacco: advice to quit, an offer of counseling and medicine, and a quit plan agreed by shared decision
Blood pressure: validated home monitoring, twice morning and evening for seven days, before a diagnosis is made
Privacy: a restricted chart with audited access, documentation kept to what care requires, and a choice of therapist, including a Black clinician if he prefers

Depression and insomnia: weekly cognitive behavioral therapy with CBT for insomnia (fixed rising time, a sleep window, no work in bed), respecting his faith; sertraline 25 mg daily for a week, then 50 mg, by shared decision; no hypnotic
A sustainable work plan: one full day a week without work, no more than two speeches a day, delegation of travel and correspondence, and a two-week break in the summer
Varenicline 0.5 mg daily for three days, twice daily for four days, then 1 mg twice daily for twelve weeks, with a quit date on day eight and weekly telephone counseling; mood and sleep watched

Stage 1 hypertension at low estimated risk: lifestyle treatment (sodium below 1,500 to 2,300 mg a day, DASH-style eating, 150 minutes of activity a week, weight loss, no tobacco), home readings, urine albumin and a fundus examination; medicine if home readings stay at or above 130/80 after three to six months
Depression remission (PHQ-9 below 5) by six months
Sleep of at least six and a half hours on most nights, with an Insomnia Severity Index below 10
About seven hours on most nights; ISI 7 at twenty-three weeks
Smoke-free, confirmed at every visit after the quit date
Smoke-free since the quit date except one lapse in June; finishing a second twelve weeks of varenicline
Home blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg with lifestyle changes
Home average 128/82 at twenty-three weeks, from 136/86
A sustainable schedule: one full day a week without work, no more than two speeches a day, and a two-week break in the summer
Kept for six weeks; two-week break taken in July

list.item: Independent and working full time, but drained after speaking, unable to rest on days off, and forgetting small things [S]

Composed, courteous and eloquent; tired; mood low, affect constricted but warm; speaks calmly of the likelihood that he will be killed, without any wish to die; no suicidal ideation, intent or plan; no psychotic features; insight and judgment good [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-04-07: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. No suicidal ideation, intent, plan or past suicide attempt. He expects that he may be killed and has accepted the risk, which is a realistic appraisal, not a wish to die. Risk factors weighed: an impulsive act of self-injury in grief at twelve, an anonymous letter urging him to end his life, depression, insomnia and isolation of leadership. Outpatient care with a safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number, and review at every visit [S]
